identification.summary: Operation Red Signature is the name Trend Micro gave to a 2018 information-theft supply chain attack against organizations in South Korea, in which attackers compromised the update server of an unnamed remote support solutions provider and used it to deliver 9002 RAT to selected targets [S1][S2]. The malware was signed with the provider's stolen code-signing certificate, and the update server was configured to serve malicious files only to clients in the IP ranges of targeted organizations [S1][S3]. Trend Micro worked with South Korean firm IssueMakersLab on the analysis [S1][S3].
identification.firstObserved: 2018-04 (a ShiftDoor sample signed with the stolen certificate dated 2018-04-08, so the certificate may have been stolen as early as April 2018 per Trend Micro; campaign discovered around end of July 2018) [S1][S3]
identification.notes: Trend Micro reported a separate GandCrab ransomware phishing campaign against South Korean targets in the same period; it is not part of Operation Red Signature [S4]. In 2021 Avast reported a backdoor on a US federal commission network whose second-stage oci.dll shared markers with an Operation Red Signature sample (rcview40u.dll); Avast did not name the actor, so this is a code-overlap lead and not a merged cluster [S5][S6]. The source set does not state the vendor of the compromised update server.

attribution.basis: The cited reporting does not attribute Operation Red Signature to a named actor or state; the encyclopedia's CN country tag is an upstream import (MISP Galaxy) that the sources reviewed here do not substantiate. Avast stated it could not attribute the 2021 US commission intrusion and only noted code overlap with Operation Red Signature [S5][S6].

objectives: Trend Micro characterized the campaign as information-theft driven [S1][S3]. The follow-on IIS 6 WebDAV exploit (CVE-2017-7269) and SQL database password dumper point to interest in web server and database data [S3].

targeting.notes: Targets were organizations in South Korea; the update server delivered malicious files only to clients within the IP ranges of the targeted organizations [S1][S3]. The specific victim organizations and sectors were not identified in the sources reviewed.

capabilities.summary: Supply chain compromise of a remote support provider's update server, with theft of the vendor's code-signing certificate to sign malware, and IP-range-conditioned delivery so only chosen victims received payloads [S1][S3]. Payload was 9002 RAT, reportedly compiled 2018-07-17 and configured to go inactive by 2018-07-31, which suggests a short operational window [S2][S3]. 9002 RAT also installed an IIS 6 WebDAV exploit (CVE-2017-7269) and an SQL password dumper [S3]. Security Affairs reported a C2 server at 66.42.37.101 [S2]. Avast's later finding of oci.dll samples abusing WinDivert for traffic monitoring, with a decryptor resembling Operation Red Signature code, suggests the tooling or its source may have been reused [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: Certificate theft
campaigns.summary: A ShiftDoor sample signed with the compromised vendor certificate dated 2018-04-08 led Trend Micro to assess the certificate may have been stolen as early as April 2018 [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: Update-server compromise and 9002 RAT delivery
campaigns.summary: Attackers delivered signed 9002 RAT through the remote support provider's update process to targeted South Korean organizations; the RAT was compiled 2018-07-17 and set to go inactive by 2018-07-31 [S2][S3]. Trend Micro discovered the attacks around end of July [S1].

campaigns.name: Public reporting in South Korea
campaigns.summary: South Korean media reported the attack on 2018-08-06, and Trend Micro published its analysis as Operation Red Signature [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: Avast report: US commission backdoor with code overlap
campaigns.summary: Avast reported backdoor files masquerading as oci.dll on the network of a small US federal commission; the second-version oci.dll shared markers with Operation Red Signature's rcview40u.dll. Avast could not attribute the activity and the victim did not engage [S5][S6].

diamond.capability: 9002 RAT, CVE-2017-7269 IIS 6 WebDAV exploit, SQL password dumper, stolen code-signing certificate, conditional update-server delivery [S3].
diamond.infrastructure: A compromised remote support provider update server; reported C2 at 66.42.37.101 [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Organizations in South Korea selected by IP range [S1][S3].
diamond.technology: Remote support software update mechanism, code-signing trust, IIS 6 WebDAV and SQL database servers [S3].

gaps: Actor identity, sponsor and any vendor aliases are not stated in the sources reviewed; MISP Galaxy country tag CN unverified.
Name of the compromised remote support vendor and the victim organizations/sectors are not identified in the sources reviewed.
Trend Micro primary report and Avast primary report could not be opened (fetch unavailable); details rely on search-result excerpts and press coverage, and exact publication dates should be verified.
Relationship between the 2018 campaign and the 2021 Avast US commission intrusion is code overlap only; shared operator not established.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: the relevant environment is trusted third-party software update channels (remote support tools) and the web/database servers of targeted organizations [S3]. Step 3 (adversary): unattributed, with demonstrated capability to compromise a vendor update server, steal and abuse a code-signing certificate, and gate payloads by victim IP range [S1][S3]. MLCOA: further selective supply chain delivery of RATs against a limited victim set to collect web server and database data [S3]. MDCOA: reuse of the tooling against non-Korean government networks, as the 2021 Avast code-overlap finding suggests [S5][S6]. Candidate indicators: signed binaries from the vendor certificate outside normal release cadence, updates delivered only to some IP ranges, CVE-2017-7269 exploitation of IIS 6, oci.dll sideload anomalies with WinDivert use [S3][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: inventory remote support and auto-update software on mission networks and verify update integrity beyond signature checks, since the signature itself was stolen [S1][S3]. Authorities: defensive response on DODIN-owned systems falls to the owning network operators; vendor and allied (e.g., ROK) coordination goes through established intelligence and legal channels. Mission assurance: prioritize legacy IIS 6 and SQL servers and segment remote support tooling [S3]. Coordination: share indicators with allied partners and the affected vendor, and note that victims may not engage, as with the US commission in 2021 [S5].

provenance.importedSummary: The threat actors compromised the update server of a remote support solutions provider to deliver a remote access tool called 9002 RAT to their targets of interest through the update process. They carried this out by first stealing the company’s certificate then using it to sign the malware. They also configured the update server to only deliver malicious files if the client is located in the range of IP addresses of their target organisations.
